key_insight: LLM agents can act as a practical natural-language layer for home energy scheduling, achieving near-optimal appliance plans when connected to real pricing, weather, and generation data.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a deployable path for smarter HEMS interfaces that lower user friction while preserving cost savings, demand-response flexibility, and constraint handling.
method: Built a tool-calling ReAct agent for multi-appliance scheduling.
Integrated live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth.
evidence_signal: Across tariff, conflict, solar co-optimization, and week-long deployment tests, native function-calling models reached 100% scheduling success and captured 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Reliability drops sharply with text-parsed action interfaces, so robust function calling and constraint validation are critical for real deployments.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
